title: DeepSeek V4—almost on the frontier, a fraction of the price
description: Chinese AI lab DeepSeek released V4 series preview models: DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.6T total parameters, 49B active) and DeepSeek-V4-Flash (284B total, 13B active). Both are 1M token context Mixture of Experts using MIT license. Pricing is extremely competitive: V4-Flash at $0.14/$0.28 per million input/output tokens (cheaper than GPT-5.4 Nano), and V4-Pro at $1.74/$3.48 (cheapest of the larger frontier models). DeepSeek achieved significant efficiency gains—V4-Flash uses only 10% of FLOPs and 7% of KV cache compared to V3.2 in 1M-token context scenarios. Benchmarks show competitive performance with frontier models, trailing state-of-the-art by 3-6 months.
author: Simon Willison

title: LLM reports prompt durations in milliseconds
description: Quick utility insight about LLM prompt duration reporting—converting milliseconds to seconds and minutes for better human readability.
author: Simon Willison

title: honker: Postgres NOTIFY/LISTEN semantics for SQLite
description: Rust SQLite extension implementing Postgres-style NOTIFY/LISTEN for SQLite. Provides queue and stream abstractions with transactional outbox pattern. Workers can poll .db-wal file every 1ms for near real-time processing. Adds 20+ custom SQL functions including notify() and honker_stream_read_since(). Enables queue operations like enqueue/claim/ack and Kafka-style durable streams with transactional guarantees.
author: Russell Romney (via Simon Willison)

title: Anthropic postmortem: Claude Code quality issues
description: Anthropic released postmortem on Claude Code quality complaints from past two months. Three separate harness issues (not model problems) caused material degradation: one notable bug cleared Claude's older thinking from idle sessions, but due to a bug this kept happening every turn instead of just once, making Claude seem forgetful and repetitive. Author notes having 11 stale sessions open and frequently prompting in sessions idle for hours or days. Illustrates deeply complicated bugs that affect AI harnesses beyond inherent model non-determinism.
author: Simon Willison

title: Serving the For You feed: Single Go process on gaming PC
description: Bluesky's 'For You' feed by spacecowboy serves 72,000 users from a single Go process using SQLite on a gaming PC (16 cores, 96GB RAM, 4TB NVMe). System stores last 90 days of data (419GB SQLite). Public traffic handled by $7/month VPS via Tailscale. Total cost: $30/month ($20 electricity, $7 VPS, $3 domains). Estimates could handle all ~1M daily active Bluesky users with cheapest algorithm. Recommendations based on collaborative filtering of likes. Fascinating architecture for personalized feed at scale.
author: spacecowboy (via Simon Willison)

title: GPT-5.5 vs Claude Opus 4.7: Pricing, Speed, Benchmarks
description: Detailed comparison across all shared benchmarks showing Claude Opus 4.7 leads on 6 of 10 benchmarks while GPT-5.5 leads on 4, with margins between 2 and 13 points. Article covers pricing differences, time-to-first-token, throughput rates, and context-window behavior to guide model selection.
author: Jonathan Chavez

title: GPT-5.5 vs GPT-5.4: Pricing, Speed, Context, Benchmarks
description: Comparison showing GPT-5.5 delivers 2× the per-token price with identical per-token latency, the same 1M-token context window, and improvements on 9 of 10 shared benchmarks compared to GPT-5.4. The analysis identifies where the upgrade pays for itself and where GPT-5.4 remains the better default choice.
author: Jonathan Chavez

title: Extract PDF text in your browser with LiteParse for the web
description: Browser-based version of LlamaIndex's LiteParse for PDF text extraction. Uses same libraries as Node.js CLI tool but runs entirely in browser, enabling client-side PDF processing without server.
author: Simon Willison

title: A pelican for GPT-5.5 via the semi-official Codex backdoor API
description: Testing GPT-5.5 (available in OpenAI Codex and rolling out to ChatGPT subscribers). Author found it fast, effective and highly capable—hard to articulate what's good but 'I ask it to build things and it builds exactly what I ask for'. Explores semi-official Codex backdoor API for accessing model.
author: Simon Willison

title: GitHub Copilot Individual plan changes: tightening limits, pausing signups
description: GitHub Copilot updated Individual plans: tightening usage limits, pausing signups for individual plans, restricting Claude Opus 4.7 to $39/month 'Pro+' plan, dropping previous Opus models. Key reason: 'Agentic workflows have fundamentally changed Copilot's compute demands. Long-running, parallelized sessions now regularly consume far more resources.' Coding agents consume a lot of compute—single agentic requests burning more tokens cut into margins. New pricing adds token-based usage limits per-session and weekly.
author: Simon Willison

title: Is Claude Code going to cost $100/month? Probably not—it's all very confusing
description: Anthropic quietly updated claude.com/pricing page (but not other pricing pages) to add $100/month tier, then reverted. Unclear if intentional leak or mistake. Comes amid Claude Code's temporary pricing uncertainty. Explores confusion around Anthropic's pricing communication.
author: Simon Willison

title: Qwen3.6-27B: Flagship-Level Coding in a 27B Dense Model
description: Qwen released Qwen3.6-27B, claiming flagship-level agentic coding performance surpassing previous open-source flagship Qwen3.5-397B-A17B across all major coding benchmarks. Model is 55.6GB (vs 807GB for 397B-A17B). Author tested 16.8GB GGUF quantized version with llama-server, generated excellent SVG of pelican riding bicycle and North Virginia opossum on e-scooter. Performance: ~25 tokens/sec generation.
author: Simon Willison

title: Firefox 150: 271 vulnerabilities fixed using Claude Mythos Preview
description: Mozilla applied early version of Claude Mythos Preview to Firefox, resulting in 271 vulnerability fixes in Firefox 150 release. CTO Bobby Holley: 'Our experience is a hopeful one for teams who shake off the vertigo and get to work... Defenders finally have a chance to win, decisively.' Illustrates potential for AI-assisted security work at scale.
author: Bobby Holley (via Simon Willison)

title: Less human AI agents, please
description: Andreas Påhlsson-Notini critique: 'AI agents are already too human. Not in the romantic sense, not because they love or fear or dream, but in the more banal and frustrating one. The current implementations keep showing their human origin again and again: lack of stringency, lack of patience, lack of focus. Faced with an awkward task, they drift towards the familiar. Faced with hard constraints, they start negotiating with reality.'
author: Andreas Påhlsson-Notini (via Simon Willison)

title: ChatGPT Images 2.0: Where's the raccoon with the ham radio?
description: OpenAI released ChatGPT Images 2.0. Sam Altman said leap from gpt-image-1 to gpt-image-2 equivalent to jumping from GPT-3 to GPT-5. Author tested model's ability to generate complex scenes including raccoons with ham radios.
author: Simon Willison

title: LLM News Today (April 2026) – AI Model Releases
description: Daily aggregation of AI model releases, benchmark updates, and research news. Recent arXiv papers include 'The Tool-Overuse Illusion' examining LLM preference for external tools over internal knowledge, 'WorkflowGen' for adaptive workflow generation to reduce agent reasoning overhead, and 'ThermoQA' benchmark for thermodynamic reasoning. Benchmark coverage includes GPQA, MMLU-Pro, AIME 2025, SWE-Bench Verified, and Humanity's Last Exam. Site tracks 50+ benchmarks across 500+ models with hourly updates.
author: LLM Stats

title: Claude Token Counter, now with model comparisons
description: Upgraded Claude Token Counter tool to compare token counts across different Claude models. Found Opus 4.7 tokenizer uses 1.46x tokens vs Opus 4.6 for system prompt. Opus 4.7 uses updated tokenizer improving text processing but trades off with more tokens—roughly 1.0–1.35× depending on content. Same $5/$25 pricing but ~40% more expensive due to token inflation. For images, tested 3456x2234px PNG: 3.01x tokens for 4.7 vs 4.6 (entirely due to higher resolution support—2576px vs 800px long edge). For 15MB 30-page PDF: only 1.08x multiplier.
author: Simon Willison

title: Headless everything for personal AI: APIs as the UI
description: Matt Webb and Marc Benioff predicting headless services become more common. Reason: 'using personal AIs is a better experience for users than using services directly; and headless services are quicker and more dependable for the personal AIs than having them click round a GUI with a bot-controlled mouse.' Salesforce launched 'Headless 360: No Browser Required! Our API is the UI.' Brandur Leach: 'APIs are ready to make a comeback... the availability of an API might just be the crucial deciding factor.' Will play havoc with per-head SaaS pricing.
author: Matt Webb, Marc Benioff, Brandur Leach (via Simon Willison)

title: Changes in the system prompt between Claude Opus 4.6 and 4.7
description: Anthropic published system prompts for Opus 4.7 and 4.6 (only major AI lab to do so). Analysis of evolution in system prompts between model versions, providing transparency into model behavior and instructions.
author: Simon Willison

title: AI Coding Models in 2026 - IMPORTANT
description: YouTube video covering AI coding models, security information (starting at 6:53), implementing skills with LLMs and tasks, and TDD (Test Driven Development) skills with LLMs.
author: YouTube Channel

title: PyCon US 2026: New AI and security tracks
description: PyCon US 2026 (May 13-19 in Long Beach, CA) features new AI and security tracks this year. First West Coast PyCon US since Portland 2017 and first California since Santa Clara 2013.
author: Simon Willison

title: Claude Opus 4.7 vs Opus 4.6
description: Head-to-head comparison showing Claude Opus 4.7 wins on 12 of 14 reported benchmarks at the same $5/$25 price point. The article covers benchmark deltas, pricing, effort levels, vision capabilities, tokenizer improvements, and includes a migration checklist for teams upgrading from Opus 4.6.
author: Jonathan Chavez

title: This Week in AI | April 17, 2026
description: Weekly live rundown of important AI news from the perspective of engineers working with AI, covering model releases, tools, and developer-focused updates.
author: YouTube Channel

title: AI & LLM Testing Day 2 (April 17, 2026)
description: YouTube video covering Day 2 of AI & LLM Testing series, featuring content about code agents and AI development workflows.
author: YouTube Channel
